passages.title: Asking for Directions Politely
passages.body: When you visit a new place, you will often need to ask for directions. Knowing how to ask politely can make a big difference. First, get the person's attention in a friendly way. A simple "Excuse me" is the best start. Then, use a polite question form, such as "Could you please tell me where the station is?" instead of a direct "Where is the station?" A polite question shows respect and makes people more willing to help. If the directions are not clear, you can politely ask the person to repeat them. Finally, don't forget to say "Thank you" before you leave. These small steps can turn a stranger into a helpful friend and make your trip much smoother.

passages.title: At the Information Desk
passages.body:
Tourist: Excuse me, could you please tell me how I can get to the City Library?
Clerk: Of course. Go straight along this street and turn left at the second corner. It's next to the post office.
Tourist: Thank you. Do you know if the library is open on Sundays?
Clerk: Yes, it is, but only in the morning, from nine to twelve.
Tourist: Great. One more question — is there a place to eat near the library?
Clerk: There's a nice cafe across from it. The sandwiches there are very popular.
Tourist: That's very helpful. Thank you so much!
Clerk: You're welcome. Enjoy your day!

passages.title: A Kind Stranger
passages.body: Last summer, I traveled to a small town alone for the first time. After I got off the train, I felt completely lost. The streets all looked the same, and I could not find my hotel. I was too shy to ask anyone at first. Finally, I saw an old man sitting on a bench. I walked up to him and said, "Excuse me, sir. Could you please tell me how I can get to the Sunshine Hotel?" He smiled warmly and stood up. Instead of just pointing, he walked with me for five minutes until we reached the hotel gate. I thanked him again and again. That day, I learned that being polite and brave enough to ask can turn a stranger into a friend.

passages.title: A Letter Before the Trip
passages.body: Dear Mike, I'm so glad you are coming to visit my city next month! Let me give you some useful tips. When you arrive at the airport, you can take the airport bus to the city center. If you are not sure which bus to take, just ask the staff politely. You can say, "Could you please tell me which bus goes to the city center?" People here are friendly and will be happy to help. If you get lost in the streets, don't worry. Look for a police officer or go into a shop and ask, "Excuse me, do you know where I am on this map?" Remember to say "thank you" afterwards. I'm sure you will enjoy your trip. See you soon! Yours, Anna

passages.title: Why Politeness Matters When Asking
passages.body: When we need help from a stranger, the way we ask is very important. Some people think that asking directly, like "Where is the station?", saves time. However, a direct question can sound rude. A polite question, such as "Could you please tell me where the station is?", shows respect. People are more willing to help someone who is polite. Politeness also makes the other person feel comfortable. In a new place, you may need to ask many people for help, so good manners can make your trip much smoother. Of course, being polite does not mean using long, difficult sentences. A simple "Excuse me" at the beginning is often enough. In short, a little politeness goes a long way.

passages.title: City Information Guide
passages.body: Welcome to Greentown! Here is some useful information for visitors. TOURIST CENTER: Located at No. 5 Center Street, open from 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. The staff can answer your questions and give you a free map. RESTROOMS: Public restrooms can be found in the Central Park and near the bus station. ASKING FOR HELP: If you need directions, look for people wearing blue "Helper" shirts. They are city volunteers. You can also ask shop workers politely. USEFUL TIP: Save the city emergency number 110 in your phone. ENJOY YOUR STAY: Greentown is a safe and friendly city. Don't be afraid to ask for help — we are always glad to welcome visitors!
